newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese rules limit foreign copyright firms.
newsitem.headline: Chinese rules limit foreign copyright firms.

text.p: China issued new regulations on Friday requiring foreign copyright agencies to apply for permanent offices in Beijing and limiting their permanent staff to five.
The rules would improve management of foreign copyright agencies operating in China, the Xinhua news agency quoted the State Copyright Administration as saying.
Holders of foreign copyrights and foreign agencies must be recognised by the administration before they can apply to open permanent offices in Beijing, it said.

After obtaining administration approval, foreign firms must apply to the State Administration for Industry and Commerce to set up a permanent office, will be limited to one representative in Beijing with a maximum permanent staff of five, it said.
The representative can stay for three years, it said.
China has already approved several foreign copyright offices in Beijing, including one from a U.S. film group, Xinhua said, but gave no details.
U.S. indignation at widespread copyright piracy in China took the two countries to the brink of a multibillion dollar trade war last year.

Western computer and music industry executives believe a Chinese crackdown on pirates has had some success since the signing of a Sino-U.S. accord that averted trade war, but say many counterfeit production lines remain in operation.
